rows.query: What happens if a connector loses its authorisation?

retrieved.text: Connectors and Integrations. Each connector exposes its own event categories, and the names follow the source service. The GitHub connector can emit review requested, mention, assigned, workflow failed, and release published. The Jira and Linear connectors can emit assigned, mentioned, status changed, comment added, and due date approaching. The Gmail and Outlook connectors can emit direct message, thread reply, and label matched, where label matched lets a user forward only mail carrying a specific label. Calendar connectors emit event starting soon, event changed, and invitation received. Chat connectors emit direct message, channel mention, and keyword matched. When a connector's authorisation expires or is revoked, Unopsis marks it as degraded rather than deleting it, retains its existing notifications, and emails the owner. A degraded connector is retried on a backoff schedule for seven days. If it has not recovered after seven days it moves to a disabled state and stops being retried, but its historical notifications remain readable for as long as the plan's retention window allows. Reauthorising a disabled connector restores it without losing history, and no notifications are backfilled for the period during which it was disabled.

Connectors and Integrations. A connector is an authenticated link between Unopsis and one external service. Unopsis currently ships connectors for Gmail, Outlook, Slack, Discord, GitHub, GitLab, Jira, Linear, Notion, Trello, Zendesk, PagerDuty, and Google Calendar. Each connector is implemented against the source service's official API and uses OAuth where the provider supports it, so Unopsis never stores a user's password for a third party service. Adding a connector takes two steps: authorise Unopsis in the provider's consent screen, then choose which event categories from that provider should produce notifications. The second step matters, because most providers emit far more events than any person wants to read.

The Free plan retains notifications for seven days, the Pro plan for ninety days, and the Team plan for three hundred and sixty five days. When a notification passes its retention window it is deleted permanently rather than archived, and deletion is not reversible. Pinned notifications are exempt from retention and are kept until the user unpins or deletes them. Users may delete any notification at any time, and may delete their entire account from account settings, which removes all notifications, connectors, and billing records within thirty days. Unopsis stores the minimum necessary content from each source. For most connectors this means the title, the author, the timestamp, a short preview of the body, and a deep link back to the original item. Unopsis does not store full email bodies, full issue descriptions, or attachments. Attachment previews are generated at display time by requesting the item from the source service using the user's own authorisation, and are limited to five megabytes. This design means that revoking a connector immediately removes Unopsis's ability to read any new content from that service, even for notifications already in the inbox.

rows.query: How many times does a failed webhook get retried?

retrieved.text: Technical Architecture. Notification deduplication happens at write time. Each incoming event is reduced to a fingerprint composed of the connector identifier, the source item identifier, and the event category. If a fingerprint already exists within a twenty four hour window, the incoming event updates the existing notification's timestamp rather than creating a second row. This matters because several source APIs re deliver the same event when an item is edited, and without deduplication a single active pull request could produce dozens of near identical entries in a user's inbox over the course of a day. The public API is REST over HTTPS and is available on the Pro and Team plans.
